title: Why is most of an iceberg underwater?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How much of an iceberg is underwater?

explain.say: Icebergs are huge chunks of freshwater ice that break off glaciers and ice sheets. They float, but only about a tenth of an iceberg shows above the sea.

draw.text: Why is most of an iceberg underwater?

explain.say: Gravity pulls the iceberg down with its weight. As it sinks into the water, it pushes water out of the way.

The water pushes back up with a force called buoyancy, equal to the weight of the water pushed aside. Ice is about 90 percent as dense as seawater, so it floats when about 90 percent of it is under water.
That is where the saying the tip of the iceberg comes from: most of it is hidden. The hidden ice is why icebergs are so dangerous to ships, like the Titanic in 1912.

faq.a: Ice is less dense than seawater, because water molecules freeze into an open pattern with gaps. Anything less dense than water floats.
asks: Why does an iceberg not sink?

faq.q: How much of an iceberg is underwater?
faq.a: About 90 percent. Ice is roughly 90 percent as dense as seawater, so it sinks until the water it pushes aside weighs as much as the whole iceberg.
asks: What does tip of the iceberg mean?

faq.a: Buoyancy is the upward push of a liquid on something in it. It equals the weight of the liquid pushed aside, so an object floats when that push matches its weight.
No. Icebergs break off glaciers and ice sheets made from snow that fell over thousands of years, so they are freshwater ice, even though they float in the salty sea.
The biggest ever measured, B-15, broke off Antarctica in 2000 and covered about 11,000 square kilometres, about the size of Jamaica.

facts: Iceberg B-15, which broke off Antarctica's Ross Ice Shelf in 2000, covered about 11,000 square kilometres.
The Titanic sank in April 1912 after hitting an iceberg in the North Atlantic.

quiz.say: About how much of an iceberg is hidden below the water?
quiz.show: The part of an iceberg below water is about…
quiz.why: Ice is about 90 percent as dense as seawater, so about 90 percent of it sinks below the surface before it floats.

wrong.1: About 10 percent is the part that shows above the water.
wrong.2: Half would only be true for something half as dense as seawater.
